about.title: Benicia Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Benicia's mix of industrial, port-adjacent, and commercial worksites means workplace injuries here can look very different depending on the job — a warehouse fall near I-780, a delivery mishap along Lake Herman Road, or equipment failure at a refinery-linked site. In most cases, California workers' compensation is the exclusive path against your employer, regardless of fault. But when a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment manufacturer contributed to the accident, a separate third-party injury claim may be possible alongside your workers' comp benefits. LawProactive doesn't charge for this connection and isn't a law firm — we simply help injured workers in Benicia get in touch with an independent attorney who can review the details of the incident, explain your options, and help you understand what deadlines and reporting steps apply to your situation. Every workplace injury case has its own facts, so getting a knowledgeable second opinion early can matter.

whyChoose.title: Why Benicia Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding the Exclusive Remedy Rule
items.desc: California generally requires injured workers to go through workers' compensation rather than suing their employer directly. An independent attorney can help you understand how this applies to your specific job injury and whether other options exist.

items.title: Spotting Third-Party Claims
items.desc: If a subcontractor, equipment maker, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may have a separate claim outside the workers' comp system. This distinction can be easy to miss without legal guidance, and it can affect the compensation available to you.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers who report an injury. An attorney can help you understand your rights if you feel you've faced pushback after reporting a workplace incident.

items.question: I was hurt at a job site near I-680 in Benicia — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' compensation is the exclusive remedy against your employer, so that's typically the first step regardless of fault. However, if a third party — like a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, or another driver — contributed to your injury, you may also have a separate claim. An independent attorney can look at the specifics of your incident and explain which paths may apply.

items.question: How long do I have to report a workplace injury in California?
items.answer: You generally need to notify your employer within 30 days of the injury to preserve your workers' compensation rights. If a third-party claim is also involved, that claim typically carries a separate two-year deadline. Because these timelines can overlap and vary by circumstance, it's worth speaking with an attorney sooner rather than later.

items.question: My employer told me not to report my injury — what should I do?
items.answer: Retaliation against workers for reporting an on-the-job injury is illegal under California law. If you've experienced this in Benicia or anywhere else, an independent attorney can help you understand your options and next steps. LawProactive can connect you with one at no cost.
